source_refs.note: Exercise 12.3, Question 6: continuity of a piecewise cost function at x = 100 (book p.236). Answer key PDF 310: yes.

blocks.prompt: 6 The factory's cost function is given as: \[C(x) = \begin{cases} 10x + 500, & x \le 100 \\ 12x + 300, & x > 100 \end{cases}\]Is the cost function continuous at \(x = 100\)?
blocks.explanation:
A continuity question for a two-piece cost function.
We must check whether the two cost formulas give the same cost at \(x = 100\).
Plan: find \(C(100)\), the LHL and the RHL, then test the three conditions.
steps:
Given: \(C(x) = 10x + 500\) for \(x \le 100\), \(12x + 300\) for \(x > 100\).
To find: whether \(C\) is continuous at \(x = 100\).
Method: \(C\) is continuous at \(x = c\) when (i) \(C(c)\) is defined, (ii) \(\lim_{x \to c} C(x)\) exists (LHL = RHL), (iii) \(\lim_{x \to c} C(x) = C(c)\).

Condition (i): find \(C(100)\)
\[C(100) = 10(100) + 500\]
\[= 1000 + 500 = 1500\]
Why: \(x \le 100\) includes 100, so the first formula is used.

Left hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 100^-} C(x) = \lim_{x \to 100^-} (10x + 500)\]
\[= 1500\]
Why: Below 100 units the first formula applies.

Right hand limit
\[\lim_{x \to 100^+} C(x) = \lim_{x \to 100^+} (12x + 300)\]
\[= 1200 + 300 = 1500\]
Why: Above 100 units the second formula applies.

Conditions (ii) and (iii)
\[\text{LHL} = \text{RHL} = 1500 = C(100)\]
Why: All three conditions hold, so \(C\) is continuous at \(x = 100\): the cost does not jump when production passes 100 units.

Check
\[C(99) = 990 + 500 = 1490\]
\[C(101) = 1212 + 300 = 1512\]
Why: Costs just below and just above 100 units are both close to 1500.
blocks.final_answer: Yes. \(C\) is continuous at \(x = 100\) (LHL \(=\) RHL \(= C(100) = 1500\))
